The weight-based base fee is under C.R.S. 42-3-306.

The yearly specific ownership tax is figured from 85% of the original MSRP: 2.1% in the first year, then 1.5%, 1.2%, 0.9%, 0.45% for years five through nine, and $3 from the tenth year. The estimate includes it for passenger vehicles from the MSRP you enter ($30,000 if blank).
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with your county motor vehicle office or the Colorado Department of Revenue.
The local range is from the July 2026 DR 1002 and changes each January 1 and July 1. Home-rule cities collect their own tax and DR 1002 suggests confirming their rates with the city.
County fees, the emissions-area fee, and license plate materials are not included, and motorcycles are shown without the specific ownership tax. The DMV’s registration fee estimator gives your total.
Whether plug-in hybrids pay the $63.05 road usage fee is not spelled out on the DMV page; the estimate includes it.

Registration shown is the statewide fees for a car between 2,001 and 5,000 lbs, with the weight-based base fee figured at 3,500 lbs. It includes the $19.30 road safety surcharge ($23 from September 1, 2027).
Plug-in electric vehicles pay a $63.05 road usage fee, plus the electric motor vehicle road usage fee of $26 ($13 for plug-in hybrids) from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. The estimate includes both.

Colorado’s sources do not say whether its electric vehicle and plug-in hybrid fees apply to motorcycles, so the estimate leaves them out for a motorcycle. Confirm with your county motor vehicle office.

faqs.question: What is the sales tax on a private car purchase in Colorado?
faqs.answer: The state rate is 2.9%, plus the city, county, and special district taxes where you live and register the car. On a private sale, you pay them all to the county clerk at registration.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in lower the tax in Colorado?
faqs.answer: Yes. If you trade in a vehicle you own as part of buying another, its fair market value is excluded from the taxable price, as long as the traded vehicle is subject to registration.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in Colorado?
faqs.answer: The title transfer fee is $7.20. A lender adding a lien pays $40 in lien filing fees plus the title fee.

faqs.question: What is the Colorado specific ownership tax?
faqs.answer: It is a yearly tax paid with registration, in place of property tax. It is figured from 85% of the original MSRP: 2.1% in the first year, 1.5% in the second, 1.2% in the third, 0.9% in the fourth, 0.45% in years five through nine, and $3 from the tenth year. The calculator includes it for passenger vehicles from the MSRP you enter.

faqs.question: I am moving to Colorado. Do I pay sales tax on my car?
faqs.answer: No use tax applies to a vehicle you acquired outside Colorado and brought with you when you became a resident. Register it within 90 days, with a VIN inspection for an out-of-state title.

faqs.question: Is a gifted vehicle taxed in Colorado?
faqs.answer: The person receiving a gift owes no sales or use tax, but the giver must have paid tax on their own purchase, and the county clerk needs the receipts before registering it. Taking over a loan on the vehicle is a taxable sale.

faqs.question: How long do I have to register a private vehicle purchase in Colorado?
faqs.answer: Register within 60 days of the sale. After that, late fees are $25 for each month, up to $100.

minnesota.label: Minnesota
minnesota.localTaxNote: Minnesota’s 6.875% Motor Vehicle Sales Tax applies statewide; local sales taxes do not apply to vehicles. Some cities and counties charge a $20 local vehicle excise tax, and many counties add a wheelage tax at registration.
notes: Minnesota’s Motor Vehicle Sales Tax is 6.875% of the price, paid when the title is transferred.
A title transfer costs $36: $8.25 title fee, $12 filing fee, $2.25 technology surcharge, $10 transfer tax, and $3.50 public safety vehicle fee. Recording a lien adds $2.
Vehicles 10 or more years old that sell for under $3,000 (and have an average value under $3,000) pay a $10 tax instead.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with Minnesota Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) or the Minnesota Department of Revenue.
Minnesota’s Motor Vehicle Sales Tax is 6.875%. A trade-in allowance reduces the taxable price when the seller takes a vehicle in trade.

Plates and registration stay with the vehicle and pass to you, so the registration tax shown is what you pay at the next renewal: $10 plus 1.575% of the original MSRP, reduced by the vehicle’s age ($30 from its 11th year). Renewal filing fees and any county wheelage tax are extra.
Electric vehicles pay at least $150 a year more and plug-in hybrids at least $75, or more based on the MSRP and age.
A deputy registrar office adds a $1 local office surcharge to title transactions.
Minnesota’s sources do not say whether its electric vehicle and plug-in hybrid fees apply to motorcycles, so the estimate leaves them out for a motorcycle. Confirm with Driver and Vehicle Services.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate on a private car purchase in Minnesota?
faqs.answer: Minnesota’s Motor Vehicle Sales Tax is 6.875% of the price, paid to a deputy registrar or Driver and Vehicle Services when the title is transferred. Local sales taxes do not apply to vehicles. A vehicle 10 or more years old that sells for under $3,000 (with an average value under $3,000) pays a $10 tax instead.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private car sale in Minnesota?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Department of Revenue subtracts a trade-in allowance from the price when the seller takes a motor vehicle in trade.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in Minnesota?
faqs.answer: A title transfer is $36: the $8.25 title fee, $12 filing fee, $2.25 technology surcharge, $10 transfer tax, and $3.50 public safety vehicle fee. Recording a lien adds $2, and a deputy registrar office adds a $1 surcharge.

faqs.question: How is Minnesota vehicle registration calculated?
faqs.answer: Plates and registration stay with the vehicle. At renewal, the registration tax is $10 plus 1.575% of the original MSRP, reduced by age (95% in year 2 down to 10% in year 10), and $30 from the 11th year. Motorcycles are $10. Electric vehicles add at least $150 and plug-in hybrids at least $75.

faqs.question: Do I pay Minnesota vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: If you bought and titled the vehicle in your name in the other state at least 60 days before, no tax is due when you register it in Minnesota. Otherwise you pay Minnesota’s 6.875% tax, with credit for sales tax paid to the other state.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Minnesota?
faqs.answer: A gift between spouses, between parents and a child, or between grandparents and a grandchild is not taxed, and no affidavit is required. Inheritances and transfers between spouses in a divorce are not taxed either. Other gifts are taxed on the vehicle’s fair market value.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Minnesota?
faqs.answer: The ownership transfer must be made on the title within 10 days of the sale. A $2 late transfer penalty applies after 20 calendar days. New residents have 60 days to register their vehicles.

south-carolina.label: South Carolina
south-carolina.localTaxNote: South Carolina charges a one-time 5% Infrastructure Maintenance Fee (IMF), up to $500, instead of sales tax. Before you can register, you pay the county property tax on the vehicle, which is not included here.
notes: On a private sale, the IMF is 5% of fair market value, up to $500. Fair market value is the price less any trade-in, or the value in a used-vehicle guide the SCDMV uses, less any trade-in.
Transfers to immediate family (spouse, parents, children, brothers, sisters, grandparents, and grandchildren) and to heirs are excluded from the IMF.
The title is $15. Registration for most passenger cars is $40 for two years; motorcycles are $10. Electric vehicles add $120 and hybrids $60 every two years.
Register within 45 days of the purchase. You must pay the county property tax and bring the paid receipt to the SCDMV first.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the SCDMV.
The estimate uses the price you enter. The SCDMV may use a used-vehicle guide value instead, so the fee can differ.
County vehicle property tax, due before registration, is not included.
A vehicle first titled in another state pays a $250 IMF instead when registered here, which the estimate does not apply.
Registration is $36 instead of $40 at age 65 or with a disability.
South Carolina’s sources do not say whether its electric vehicle and plug-in hybrid fees apply to motorcycles, so the estimate leaves them out for a motorcycle. Confirm with the SCDMV.

faqs.question: What is the car tax in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: South Carolina charges a 5% Infrastructure Maintenance Fee (IMF) instead of sales tax when you first title or register a vehicle, up to $500.

faqs.question: Does South Carolina have a maximum on the vehicle fee?
faqs.answer: Yes. The IMF is capped at $500, which a vehicle valued at $10,000 or more reaches.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce the IMF on a private sale in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: Yes. Fair market value for the fee is the price, or a used-vehicle guide value, less any trade-in.

faqs.question: How much are title and registration fees in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: The title is $15. Registration for most passenger cars is $40 for two years, $10 for a motorcycle. Electric vehicles add $120 and hybrids $60 every two years. You also pay county property tax before registering.

faqs.question: I am moving to South Carolina. What do I pay?
faqs.answer: For most passenger cars, $305 at the SCDMV: the $250 IMF, the $15 title fee, and the $40 registration. You pay the county property tax first and bring the paid receipt.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxed in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: A transfer to a spouse, parent, child, brother, sister, grandparent, or grandchild is excluded from the IMF, and so is a transfer to an heir.

faqs.question: How long do I have to register a private vehicle purchase in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: Register within 45 days of the purchase date. Late registration penalties start at $10 from day 46 and rise to $75 after 135 days.

alabama.label: Alabama
alabama.localTaxNote: Alabama charges a 2% state sales tax on a vehicle bought from a private seller, plus the county and city automotive rates where you live. The licensing official collects it when you register. ALDOR's November 2026 local rate file shows combined county and city automotive rates from 0% (Monroe County outside city limits) to 5.25% (Shorter, in Macon County) where the levies can be matched to one place. Some counties split their levies by city limits, police jurisdictions, and unabated portions, and the file does not say which combine, so a few places may be higher.
notes: The 2% state tax and the local automotive rates apply to private sales under Ala. Code 40-23-101, based on where the buyer lives. Your county licensing official collects them before issuing a plate.
A vehicle taken in trade lowers the taxed price: the tax is on the price less the trade-in credit (Ala. Code 40-23-103).
The title is $15, and recording a lien (notice of security interest) is $15.
A passenger car plate is $23 a year plus a $1.25 issuance fee and any local fees; motorcycles are $15. Battery electric vehicles add $203 a year and plug-in hybrids $103 (since July 1, 2023).
Ad valorem (property) tax is collected with the registration. It depends on the vehicle's value and local millage rates, so it is not in the estimate.
Get a plate within 20 calendar days of buying the vehicle. Alabama does not require emissions testing.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with your county licensing official or the Alabama Department of Revenue (ALDOR).
The local range comes from ALDOR's November 2026 local rate file. Your county licensing official applies the exact rate for your address.
Ad valorem tax, the $1.25 issuance fee, and local issuance fees are not included. Licensing officials may also add small commissions.
Registration may be prorated to your renewal month, which is set by the first letter of your last name.
Alabama’s sources do not say whether its electric vehicle and plug-in hybrid fees apply to motorcycles, so the estimate leaves them out for a motorcycle. Confirm with the Department of Revenue.

faqs.question: What is the car sales tax in Alabama for private sales?
faqs.answer: Alabama charges a 2% state sales tax on a vehicle bought from someone who is not a licensed dealer, plus the county and city automotive rates where you live (Ala. Code 40-23-101). ALDOR's November 2026 local rate file shows combined local automotive rates from 0% to 5.25% where they can be matched to one place; a few areas that stack several county levies may be higher. You pay when you register with your county licensing official.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in lower the tax on a private sale in Alabama?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ala. Code 40-23-103 taxes the price less the credit for a vehicle taken in trade, and the section covers private (casual) sales. It only applies when the seller takes your vehicle as part of the payment.

faqs.question: How much are title and lien fees in Alabama?
faqs.answer: ALDOR lists the certificate of title fee at $15 and a notice of security interest (lien) at $15. Designated agents and licensing officials may add a $1.50 commission each, and some counties add local fees.

faqs.question: How much does registration cost in Alabama?
faqs.answer: A standard passenger car plate is $23 a year plus a $1.25 issuance fee; local fees and ad valorem tax may be added. Motorcycles are $15. Battery electric vehicles pay an extra $203 a year and plug-in hybrids $103, rates that took effect July 1, 2023. Regular hybrids that do not plug in pay no extra fee.

faqs.question: I am moving to Alabama. What do I pay?
faqs.answer: ALDOR says a non-commercial vehicle with a valid registration from another state must be registered within 30 days of entering Alabama (Ala. Code 40-12-262). If the vehicle was substantially used in another state, shown by an out-of-state registration or title, no sales or use tax is due when you first register it here. You still pay the title, registration, and ad valorem tax.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxed in Alabama?
faqs.answer: Alabama's casual sales tax is on the purchase price, and ALDOR rule 810-6-1-.150 says a transfer made as a gift is not a sale. A true gift therefore owes no sales tax, but the title and registration fees and ad valorem tax still apply. A family sale with a price is taxed like any other private sale. Ask your licensing official what proof of a gift they accept.

faqs.question: How long do I have to register a private vehicle purchase in Alabama?
faqs.answer: ALDOR says you must get a license plate within 20 calendar days of acquiring the vehicle. The title application must be completed before the registration can be processed, and the seller does not need to notarize the title assignment. Alabama liability insurance is required, and the seller keeps the old plate.

alabama.tradeInNote: Alabama taxes the price less the credit for a vehicle taken in trade, on private sales too (Ala. Code 40-23-103). Enter a trade-in only if the seller took your vehicle as part of the payment.

louisiana.label: Louisiana
louisiana.localTaxNote: Louisiana’s 5% state sales tax plus parish and municipal tax, from 2% to 8.5% in the OMV parish tax table (October 2026), is due based on where the vehicle is domiciled.
notes: Louisiana’s state sales tax is 5% (from January 1, 2025, through 2029). Parish and municipal taxes add 2% to 8.5%.
Title fees are $68.50 plus an $8 handling fee. A local fee of up to $6 may apply.
Passenger plates cost 0.1% of the sale price per year (minimum value $10,000) and are sold for two years.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Louisiana Office of Motor Vehicles (OMV) or the Louisiana Department of Revenue.
Sales tax is the 5% state rate plus parish and municipal tax (2% to 8.5%) where the vehicle is domiciled, due by the 40th day after the sale.
The title shown includes the $68.50 title fee and $8 handling fee. A local fee of up to $6 may apply.
The plate is 0.1% of the sale price per year, with a $10,000 minimum value, sold for two years ($20 minimum). A motorcycle plate is $12 and lasts four years.
Electric vehicles owe a $110 road usage fee and hybrids $60 for each year, billed later by notice.
The title assignment must be signed before a notary.
Louisiana’s sources do not say whether its electric vehicle and plug-in hybrid fees apply to motorcycles, so the estimate leaves them out for a motorcycle. Confirm with the Office of Motor Vehicles.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Louisiana for private sales?
faqs.answer: The state rate is 5% (from January 1, 2025, through 2029). Parish and municipal taxes add 2% to 8.5% depending on where the vehicle is domiciled, for a combined 7% to 13.5%.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private car sale in Louisiana?
faqs.answer: Trade-in credit applies when you buy from a dealer with a qualifying trade-in. In an even trade between two individuals, tax is due only on the difference in value.

faqs.question: Does Louisiana require a notarized bill of sale?
faqs.answer: The title must be assigned before a notary by the seller. A bill of sale showing the price must be notarized too, unless the price is written in the title assignment.

faqs.question: How much does a vehicle title cost in Louisiana?
faqs.answer: The title fee is $68.50, plus an $8 handling fee and a local fee of up to $6. Recording a lien costs $10, or $15 with a UCC-1 financing statement.

faqs.question: Do I pay Louisiana vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tax is assessed on the sale price when you title the vehicle in Louisiana. If you buy from an out-of-state seller, show proof the seller lives out of state (such as a copy of their license or a document notarized out of state), or OMV may process it as more than one transfer.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Louisiana?
faqs.answer: No sales or use tax is due on an act of donation, which is signed before a notary and two witnesses (Form DPSMV1699). Transfers by affidavit of heirship, divorce decree, or judgment of possession are also not taxed. Title, handling, and plate fees still apply.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Louisiana?
faqs.answer: Sales tax is due by the 40th day after the sale. After that, a penalty of 5% of the tax for each 30 days applies (up to 25%), plus interest.

kentucky.label: Kentucky
kentucky.localTaxNote: Kentucky charges a 6% motor vehicle usage tax statewide (KRS 138.460). Counties and cities add no sales tax to a vehicle purchase.
notes: The 6% usage tax is on the total price shown on the notarized affidavit of total consideration (Form TC 96-182), less any trade-in allowance. It cannot be less than 50% of the trade-in value of the vehicle you buy minus the trade-in value of any vehicle traded. Without the affidavit, the tax is on the average retail value in the reference manual.

Title applications are $9 and recording a lien is $12 (KRS 186A.130 and KRS 64.012, the lien fee since July 15, 2026). The $9 title fee is set in statute until January 1, 2027, when the fee moves to regulation.
Registration is $20.50 a year for a car ($11.50 state fee, $6 clerk fee, and $3 more until January 1, 2027) and $18 for a motorcycle. A $10 wildlife contribution is added unless you opt out.

Electric vehicles, including plug-in hybrids, pay an electric vehicle ownership fee. The statute sets it at $120 ($60 for electric motorcycles) and has the Department of Revenue adjust it each year; regular hybrids pay no fee.
Kentucky also bills a yearly property tax on the vehicle you own on January 1, at local rates, with your renewal. It is not part of this estimate.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with your county clerk or the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet.
The electric vehicle fee shown is the $120 statutory base. The Department of Revenue adjusts it each year, and the adjusted 2026 amount is not published on the Cabinet's fee pages.
The usage tax cannot fall below the floor set from the reference manual values, which the estimate does not apply.
Yearly vehicle property tax and the optional $10 wildlife contribution are not included.

An electric or plug-in hybrid motorcycle pays a $60 ownership fee instead (KRS 138.475). That is the base amount; the state adjusts it yearly, and the adjusted figure was not published when we checked.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle tax rate in Kentucky?
faqs.answer: Kentucky charges a 6% motor vehicle usage tax (KRS 138.460) when a vehicle is titled. There is no county or city sales tax on top of it. Your county clerk collects it with the title application.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in lower the usage tax on a private sale in Kentucky?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Department of Revenue's 2025 usage tax guide taxes the total consideration on the notarized affidavit (Form TC 96-182) less the seller's trade-in allowance. The taxed amount cannot be less than 50% of the trade-in value of the vehicle you buy minus the trade-in value of the vehicle traded.

faqs.question: How much are Kentucky title and lien fees?
faqs.answer: A title application is $9 under KRS 186A.130, which sets that fee until January 1, 2027; after that the fee is set by regulation. Recording a lien is $12 under KRS 64.012, effective July 15, 2026.

faqs.question: How much does vehicle registration cost in Kentucky?
faqs.answer: A car is $20.50 a year: the $11.50 fee in KRS 186.050, the $6 clerk fee, and $3 more under KRS 186.040 until January 1, 2027. Motorcycles are $18. Electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids also pay an ownership fee with a $120 statutory base that the Department of Revenue adjusts each year; regular hybrids pay none.

faqs.question: I am moving to Kentucky. What do I pay?
faqs.answer: The Transportation Cabinet's new resident page says to title and register within 10 days of establishing residency, and elsewhere on the same page gives 15 days to apply for registration after bringing a vehicle in; plan on 10. The 6% usage tax is due, but you get credit for tax paid to another state with a substantially identical tax (KRS 138.460). An out-of-state title needs Form TC 96-182 and a sheriff's inspection.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxed in Kentucky?
faqs.answer: Transfers between spouses, parents and children (including step-relations), and grandparents and grandchildren who are Kentucky residents are exempt from the usage tax (KRS 138.470, Form 71A101). Other gifts are taxed on the average trade-in value in the reference manual (KRS 138.450).

faqs.question: How long do I have to title a private vehicle purchase in Kentucky?
faqs.answer: Transfer the title and registration within 15 days. Bring the notarized signed title, proof of Kentucky insurance, and a Kentucky license, ID, or Social Security card to your county clerk. The seller keeps the plates (KRS 186.190).

kentucky.tradeInNote: Kentucky taxes the price on the notarized affidavit (Form TC 96-182) less the seller's trade-in allowance, but not below 50% of the trade-in value of the vehicle you buy minus the trade-in value of the vehicle traded.

oregon.label: Oregon
oregon.localTaxNote: Oregon has no sales tax on a private vehicle sale. The 0.5% vehicle use tax applies only to vehicles bought from a dealer.
notes: Oregon's title and registration fees follow the vehicle's combined MPG rating. The estimate uses the 20 to 39 MPG tier: a $106 title and $136 for two years of registration.

Other tiers: 0 to 19 MPG is $101 title and $126 registration; 40 MPG or more is $116 title and $216 registration; all-electric is $192 title and $376 registration. Motorcycles are $101 title and $88 registration.
If the vehicle already has current Oregon plates, registration is not due when the title transfers. Registration is due when the vehicle has no Oregon plates or its registration has expired.
Multnomah County adds $112 and Washington and Clackamas counties add $60 to a two-year registration.
Apply for the title within 30 days of the sale; a late transfer costs $25 (31 to 60 days) or $50 (after 60 days).
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with Oregon DMV.
The estimate uses the 20 to 39 MPG fee tier. Your vehicle's MPG rating sets the real title and registration fees.
For an electric vehicle, the estimate adds the electric registration fee but keeps the $106 title fee; the all-electric title fee is $192.
County registration fees, new plate fees ($26), and DEQ emissions test fees are not included.
Oregon’s added electric vehicle registration amount is for passenger vehicles (ORS 803.420), so the estimate does not add it to a motorcycle’s $88 two-year registration.

faqs.question: What is the car sales tax rate in Oregon for private sales?
faqs.answer: None. Oregon has no sales tax on a private vehicle sale. The 0.5% vehicle use tax applies to vehicles bought from a dealer, such as new vehicles with 7,500 miles or less that were never registered in Oregon.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in Oregon?
faqs.answer: Oregon DMV sets the title fee by MPG rating: $101 for 0 to 19 MPG, $106 for 20 to 39 MPG, $116 for 40 MPG or more, and $192 for all-electric vehicles. Motorcycles are $101. Apply within 30 days of the sale to avoid a $25 or $50 late fee.

faqs.question: How are registration fees calculated in Oregon?
faqs.answer: Registration lasts two years and also follows the MPG rating: $126 for 0 to 19 MPG, $136 for 20 to 39 MPG, and $216 for 40 MPG or more (if not enrolled in OReGO). Motorcycles are $88. Multnomah County adds $112 and Washington and Clackamas counties add $60. If the vehicle already has current Oregon plates, registration is not due at the title transfer.

faqs.question: Do electric vehicles pay extra fees in Oregon?
faqs.answer: Yes. An all-electric vehicle pays a $192 title fee and $376 for two years of registration, or $86 if enrolled in OReGO, the per-mile road usage charge program. Oregon DMV says electric vehicle fees change on July 1, 2027.

faqs.question: I am moving to Oregon. What do I pay?
faqs.answer: Within 30 days of becoming a resident, get an Oregon license and title and register your vehicle. There is no sales tax. A vehicle with an out-of-state title needs a $9 VIN inspection, and vehicles in the Portland and Medford areas may need a DEQ emissions test.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxed in Oregon?
faqs.answer: No. Oregon has no sales tax on private transfers, including gifts between family members. The title fee still applies, and registration is due if the vehicle lacks current Oregon plates.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title a private vehicle purchase in Oregon?
faqs.answer: Apply for the title within 30 days of the sale. A transfer between 31 and 60 days costs a $25 late fee, and after 60 days $50.

oregon.tradeInNote: Oregon has no sales tax on a private sale, so a trade-in does not change the estimate.

oklahoma.label: Oklahoma
oklahoma.localTaxNote: Oklahoma charges a motor vehicle excise tax of $20 on the first $1,500 of a used vehicle’s value and 3.25% of the rest, plus a 1.25% sales tax on the price. Both are statewide and paid when the title is transferred.
notes: Used vehicles pay an excise tax of $20 on the first $1,500 of value and 3.25% of the rest, plus a 1.25% sales tax on the price.
A title transfer costs $29.50: $11 title fee, $17 transfer fee, and $1.50 insurance fee. Recording a lien costs $10.
Registration depends on how many years the vehicle has been registered: $96 in years 1 to 4, down to $26 from year 17.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with Service Oklahoma or a licensed operator.
Oklahoma taxes a used vehicle at $20 on the first $1,500 of value and 3.25% of the rest (excise tax), plus 1.25% sales tax on the price.
Registration shown assumes the vehicle was first registered in its model year. A tire tax (for cars, $2.90 per tire) and, for vehicles titled in another state, a $4 VIN inspection fee are extra.
Electric vehicles pay $210 a year more and plug-in hybrids $112.

On our reading, a motorcycle pays only the Motor Fuels Tax Fee of $100 for electric or $30 for hybrid (47 O.S. 1132.7), because the other fee covers vehicles with at least four wheels (68 O.S. 6511). Confirm with Service Oklahoma.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle tax rate in Oklahoma for private sales?
faqs.answer: A used vehicle pays an excise tax of $20 on the first $1,500 of value and 3.25% of the rest, plus a 1.25% sales tax on the price. On a $15,000 car that is $458.75 excise tax plus $187.50 sales tax.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Oklahoma?
faqs.answer: Service Oklahoma figures the excise tax on the purchase price or taxable value. A private sale has no trade-in credit to apply.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in Oklahoma?
faqs.answer: A title transfer costs $29.50: the $11 title fee, $17 transfer fee, and $1.50 insurance fee. Recording a lien costs $10. A vehicle titled in another state also needs a $4 VIN inspection.

faqs.question: How are vehicle registration fees calculated in Oklahoma?
faqs.answer: Registration depends on how many years the vehicle has been registered: $96 for years 1 to 4, $86 for years 5 to 8, $66 for years 9 to 12, $46 for years 13 to 16, and $26 after that. Motorcycles are $3 more in each band. Electric vehicles add $210 a year and plug-in hybrids $112.

faqs.question: Do I pay Oklahoma vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes. Take the assigned out-of-state title, Form 701-6, your driver license, proof of Oklahoma insurance, the purchase agreement or Form 722-1, and the vehicle to Service Oklahoma or a licensed operator. You pay the same excise and sales taxes, and the vehicle needs a VIN inspection.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Oklahoma?
faqs.answer: A gift between spouses, or between a parent or stepparent and a child or stepchild, is exempt from excise tax with Form 794 (Family Affidavit). It must be a gift, not a sale, and siblings and grandparents do not qualify. Transfers under a divorce decree are also exempt.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Oklahoma?
faqs.answer: Service Oklahoma requires the title to be applied for within 2 months of obtaining ownership.

connecticut.label: Connecticut
connecticut.bookValueRule: Connecticut taxes a private sale at 6.35% (7.75% over $50,000) on the higher of the purchase price or the NADA average trade-in value.
connecticut.localTaxNote: Connecticut has no local sales tax on vehicles. Your town charges property tax on the vehicle each year; it is billed by the local tax collector and is not included here.
notes: Connecticut charges 6.35% (7.75% on vehicles over $50,000) on the higher of the purchase price or the NADA average trade-in value.
The title fee is $25 and recording a lien is $10.
Passenger registration is $120 for three years, plus a $15 Clean Air Act fee, $24 Passport to the Parks fee, and $10 administrative fee.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Connecticut DMV or the Department of Revenue Services.
A private sale is taxed at 6.35% (7.75% over $50,000) on the higher of the price or the NADA average trade-in value. The estimate uses the price you enter.
Trade-in credit applies only to purchases from a licensed dealer. Swapped vehicles are taxed on their average trade-in value.

Registration shown is for three years: $120 ($63 for motorcycles) plus the $15 Clean Air Act, $24 Passport to the Parks, and $10 administrative fees. A plate fee ($5 for new plates) and, for vehicles four model years old or newer, a $40 emissions exemption fee may apply.
Your town bills property tax on the vehicle every year. It is not included here.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Connecticut for private sales?
faqs.answer: Connecticut charges 6.35% on a private-party purchase, or 7.75% on a vehicle over $50,000. There is no local sales tax, but your town bills property tax on the vehicle each year.

faqs.question: How is the tax base determined for private sales in Connecticut?
faqs.answer: The tax is based on the NADA average trade-in value or the bill of sale price, whichever is higher. Write the purchase price on Form H-13B.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Connecticut?
faqs.answer: No. Full trade-in credit applies only when you buy from a licensed dealer. When two people swap vehicles, both pay tax on the average trade-in value.

faqs.question: How much are Connecticut vehicle title and registration fees?
faqs.answer: The title fee is $25, and a lien adds $10. Passenger registration is $120 for three years ($63 for motorcycles), plus a $15 Clean Air Act fee, $24 Passport to the Parks fee, and $10 administrative fee. New plates add $5, and vehicles four model years old or newer pay a $40 emissions exemption fee.

faqs.question: Do I pay Connecticut vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes, at 6.35% (7.75% over $50,000) when you register. You get credit for sales tax paid to another state if you show the purchase invoice and tax receipt, and pay any difference.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Connecticut?
faqs.answer: No tax is due on a transfer or sale between spouses or civil union partners, parents and children, or brothers and sisters (including through adoption), if the vehicle was registered in the family member’s name for at least 60 days and was taxed on its last sale. A gift from anyone is also tax-free with a Motor Vehicle or Vessel Gift Declaration (AU-463) signed by the giver.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Connecticut?
faqs.answer: Registration is by appointment at a DMV office. If the vehicle was registered in Connecticut before, get its emissions test within 30 days of registering to avoid a late fee. New residents have 90 days after establishing residency to transfer their registration.

utah.label: Utah
utah.localTaxNote: Utah’s 4.85% state rate plus local taxes gives combined rates from 6.35% to 10.05% (October 2026). The rate is the one for where the vehicle will be registered.
notes: Utah’s state sales tax is 4.85%; local taxes bring the combined rate to between 6.35% and 10.05%.
The title fee is $6.
Registration includes an age-based uniform fee, charged in place of property tax: $150 for model years 2024 to 2026 down to $10 for 2014 and older.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Utah DMV or the Utah State Tax Commission.
Sales tax is based on the price you actually paid, at the combined rate (6.35% to 10.05%) where the vehicle will be registered. Utah has no family exemption.

Registration shown is the $72.50 registration fee ($73.25 for motorcycles) plus the 2026 uniform age-based fee, which replaces property tax. Some counties add a $10 corridor fee or a $2 to $3 air pollution control fee.
Electric vehicles pay a $180 road usage charge for 2026, rising to $280 on January 1, 2027. Plug-in hybrids pay at least $56.50, adjusted each year for inflation.
A trade lowers the price only for a vehicle-for-vehicle trade in the same transaction.
Utah’s electric and plug-in hybrid charges are added to the fee for vehicles other than motorcycles (Utah Code 41-1a-1206), so the estimate does not add them to a motorcycle.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Utah for private sales?
faqs.answer: Utah’s state rate is 4.85%. With local taxes, combined rates run from 6.35% to 10.05% (October 2026). You pay the rate for where the vehicle will be registered, on the price you actually paid.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Utah?
faqs.answer: Only for a vehicle-for-vehicle trade that happens at the same time and is documented in the same transaction. Other trades are valued and taxed.

faqs.question: How much does a vehicle title cost in Utah?
faqs.answer: A new title is $6.

faqs.question: What is the Utah age-based vehicle fee?
faqs.answer: Utah charges a uniform age-based fee at each registration in place of property tax. For 2026, passenger vehicles pay $150 for model years 2024 to 2026, $110 for 2021 to 2023, $80 for 2018 to 2020, $50 for 2015 to 2017, and $10 for 2014 and older. Motorcycles pay $95 down to $10.

faqs.question: Do I pay Utah vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sales tax is calculated at the rate for where the vehicle will be registered in Utah, on the purchase price. A VIN inspection is required for a vehicle titled in Utah for the first time.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Utah?
faqs.answer: Utah has no sales tax exemption for family-to-family vehicle purchases. Tax is due on sales between family members, on the price actually paid.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Utah?
faqs.answer: The DMV gives no fixed deadline for a private sale, but you need the title transfer and registration before driving. New residents have 60 days to transfer their titles and registrations.

iowa.label: Iowa
iowa.localTaxNote: Iowa levies the 5% Fee for New Registration statewide in lieu of retail sales tax; local option sales taxes (LOST) do not apply to motor vehicles.
notes: Iowa assesses a 5% Fee for New Registration (FNR) on vehicle purchase price under Iowa Code § 321.105A.
Certificate of title fee is $35.00 (increased Jan 1, 2025 from $25.00); lien notation is $20.00.
Private party sales do not qualify for trade-in tax credits in Iowa; full purchase price is taxed.

Annual registration is 1% of the list price plus 40 cents per 100 lbs (Iowa Code 321.109). The value part drops to 75% after 7 model years and 50% after 9, with a $50 minimum, and the fee is a flat $50 from 12 model years (Iowa Code 321.113). The estimate uses the list price you enter ($30,000 if blank) and an assumed 3,500 lbs, which is $14 of the fee.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Iowa DOT or county treasurer.
Trade-in deductions are not permitted on private-party vehicle sales in Iowa.
Certificate of title fee is $35.00 effective 2025.

The weight part of registration assumes 3,500 lbs; every 500 lbs more or less changes the fee by $2. The current model year counts as the first model year. The value part is for passenger vehicles; motorcycles are shown at their $20 fee. The Iowa DOT fee calculator gives the exact amount.
A battery electric or plug-in hybrid motorcycle pays a $9 electric motorcycle fee instead of these fees (Iowa Code 321.117).

faqs.question: What is the sales tax on a private car purchase in Iowa?
faqs.answer: In Iowa, vehicle purchases are subject to a 5% 'Fee for New Registration' collected by your county treasurer under Iowa Code § 321.105A, replacing standard retail sales tax.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private vehicle purchase in Iowa?
faqs.answer: No. Under Iowa Code § 321.105A, trade-in deductions are not allowed for private-party sales. You must pay the 5% fee on the full purchase price.

faqs.question: How much does a vehicle title cost in Iowa?
faqs.answer: The certificate of title fee in Iowa is $35.00 (increased effective January 1, 2025). If the vehicle is financed, an additional $20.00 security interest (lien) fee applies.

faqs.question: How are Iowa annual registration fees determined?
faqs.answer: Annual registration is 1% of the vehicle’s list price plus $0.40 per 100 lbs. The value part drops to 75% after 7 model years and 50% after 9, with a $50 minimum, and the fee is a flat $50 once the vehicle is 12 model years old. The calculator figures it from the list price you enter.

faqs.question: Do I pay Iowa vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: When bringing an out-of-state private vehicle into Iowa, the state generally assesses its applicable vehicle sales or use tax (5.00%) upon titling and registration. If you previously paid sales tax in another jurisdiction, many states offer reciprocal tax credit with official proof of payment, though private-sale reciprocity rules vary by statute. Contact the Iowa motor vehicle agency to verify documentation requirements.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Iowa?
faqs.answer: Rules for vehicle transfers or gifts between family members vary significantly by state. In many states, bona fide gifts or transfers between immediate family members (such as spouses, parents, or children) may qualify for tax exemption or reduced fees if accompanied by a sworn gift affidavit or certification, whereas transfers between other relatives or involving debt assumption may remain taxable. Contact the Iowa DMV or Department of Revenue to verify eligibility and required documentation before titling.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Iowa?
faqs.answer: Titling and registration deadlines for private vehicle purchases vary by jurisdiction, typically ranging between 10 to 30 days from the date of purchase. Delaying beyond Iowa's statutory filing deadline can incur late titling penalty fees and restricts legal operation on public roadways. Check with the Iowa motor vehicle agency or your local county title office for the exact filing window and penalty schedule.

nevada.label: Nevada
nevada.localTaxNote: Private party vehicle sales in Nevada are 100% exempt from sales and use tax under NRS 372.320 ('occasional sale' exemption). However, an annual Governmental Services Tax (GST) based on the vehicle's depreciated original MSRP is collected upon registration. The estimate includes it.
notes: Nevada exempts private party vehicle sales from sales and use tax under NRS 372.320 ('occasional sale' exemption).
Certificate of title fee is $28.25 under Nevada DMV fee schedule.
Base registration tag fee is $33.00 for passenger vehicles.

Nevada collects an annual Governmental Services Tax (GST): 4% of a value set at 35% of the original MSRP. Figured under NRS 371.040 to 371.060. The estimate includes it for passenger vehicles from the MSRP you enter ($30,000 if blank).
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Nevada DMV.
Private party vehicle sales are exempt from Nevada sales tax under NRS 372.320.

The estimate includes a full year of the basic GST for passenger vehicles. The value it is figured on drops with age to 95%, 85%, 75%, 65%, 55%, 45%, 35%, 25%, then 15%, and the minimum tax is $16. The 1% Supplemental GST in Clark and Churchill counties is not included, and motorcycles are shown without the GST. The DMV’s fee calculator gives your total.
The estimate adds no electric vehicle or plug-in hybrid fee, because we found none in NRS Chapter 482 or the DMV’s fee schedule. Confirm any EV fee with the Nevada DMV.

faqs.question: Do you pay sales tax on a private car sale in Nevada?
faqs.answer: No. Under Nevada Revised Statutes (NRS 372.320), private-party vehicle sales qualify as occasional sales and are completely exempt from Nevada sales and use tax.

faqs.question: What fees do I pay when buying a car privately in Nevada?
faqs.answer: While exempt from sales tax, you must pay a $28.25 certificate of title fee, a $33.00 base passenger registration fee, and the annual Governmental Services Tax (GST) based on the vehicle's depreciated original MSRP. The estimate includes the GST for passenger vehicles.

faqs.question: How is the Nevada Governmental Services Tax (GST) calculated?
faqs.answer: The GST is calculated by taking 35% of the vehicle's original Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price (MSRP), applying an annual depreciation percentage based on age, and multiplying by the 4% GST rate. Clark and Churchill counties add a 1% Supplemental GST on the same value, which the estimate does not include.

faqs.question: Do trade-in credits apply to private car sales in Nevada?
faqs.answer: Because private-party sales in Nevada are already 0% sales tax, trade-in credits do not affect your sales tax liability.
